review_text: Had a 40-minute outage during our peak business hours with no status page update until 25 minutes in. Our own customers found out before we could tell them.
Bulk user provisioning via the admin console times out past 500 users with no error message, it just silently stops partway through.
Our dedicated TAM caught a config issue before it became an incident and walked our team through the fix on a same-day call. This is why we pay for enterprise support.
Rate limits dropped without notice in the last release, breaking our nightly batch sync job that had run reliably for two years.
SSO login intermittently fails for about 5% of our workforce with a generic error, and support keeps asking us to 'try clearing cookies' instead of escalating.
Implementation team scoped our rollout well and kept to the timeline, though the SSO setup docs assumed a level of Okta expertise most of our admins didn't have.
Invoiced for 40% more seats than we actually have provisioned. Finance has been going back and forth with billing support for three weeks now.
New webhook retry logic has been rock solid since the last update, we haven't lost a single event in two months of high volume.
Response times have crept up noticeably during our EU business hours over the past month, though your status page still shows all green.
Role-based permissions don't actually restrict what the API allows, so a 'read-only' user can still modify records through direct API calls.
Opened a Severity 1 ticket for a production-impacting bug and didn't get a human response for over six hours, well outside our contracted SLA.
SOC 2 report and security questionnaire responses were delivered fast during our procurement review, which sped up our own compliance sign-off significantly.
Migration tooling from our legacy system dropped custom field mappings silently, and we only noticed weeks later when reports came out wrong.
API is well documented overall, but the changelog doesn't clearly flag breaking changes, so we found out about a renamed field from a failed deploy.
Failover to your secondary region during last month's regional cloud outage was seamless. Our end users never even noticed.
Contract renewal terms changed with only 30 days notice on a multi-year agreement, which barely gave procurement enough time to review.
New audit log export feature made our quarterly access review go from a two-day manual process to about twenty minutes.
A penetration test flagged that an old admin API key with full permissions had never been rotated in three years and support couldn't tell us why it still worked.
Support portal ticket tracking is solid now, though the knowledge base still references UI elements that were removed two releases ago.
GraphQL endpoint returns a 200 status with an empty error array even when the mutation silently fails, making failures very hard to detect programmatically.
Dedicated onboarding engineer joined our first three sprints and unblocked integration issues in real time instead of us waiting on ticket queues.
Scheduled maintenance windows have twice run over their announced time by more than an hour, pushing into our own customer-facing hours.
Usage-based pricing dashboard is accurate but only updates once every 24 hours, making it hard to catch a usage spike before it hits our bill.
Deprovisioning an offboarded employee doesn't revoke their active API tokens, which our security team flagged as a real risk during an audit.
Escalated a data discrepancy on a Friday evening and had root cause identified and a fix deployed before Monday. Exceptional turnaround.
IP allowlisting feature works but changes take up to 15 minutes to propagate, which caused a lockout during a time-sensitive deployment window.
Pagination on the reporting API changed from offset-based to cursor-based with no deprecation period, breaking every integration that relied on the old behavior overnight.
Uptime has been genuinely excellent this quarter, only real friction is that the status page granularity doesn't break down by region.
Kickoff call was six weeks after we signed the contract, and by then two of our internal stakeholders had moved on to other projects.
Finance team was able to self-serve a mid-cycle seat increase without a single sales call, which was a refreshing change from most enterprise vendors.
Bulk export of user activity logs caps at 90 days even for enterprise accounts, forcing us to run monthly exports just to retain what compliance requires.
SCIM provisioning integration with our identity provider has worked flawlessly since setup, new hires get correct access on day one automatically.
Support quality depends heavily on which engineer picks up the ticket, some resolve issues in an hour, others need the same context re-explained twice.
Sandbox environment for testing integrations before going live has saved us from at least two production incidents this year already.
Third outage this quarter attributed to 'a third-party dependency,' but we've received no details on what's actually being done to prevent recurrence.
Data migration validation reports were detailed and caught two mapping errors before go-live that would have caused real problems downstream.
Auto-renewal clause kicked in for a legacy tier we'd already been told was being deprecated, and now we're locked in for another year at the old rate structure.
Single sign-on works well day to day, but session timeout is fixed at 8 hours platform-wide with no way for us to set a shorter policy for sensitive roles.
New delegated admin feature let us give regional IT teams scoped permissions without exposing the full global admin console. Exactly what we needed.
Our TAM changed three times in six months with no handoff notes, so we kept having to re-explain our architecture from scratch each time.
